groups.name: Fictional small towns defined by a supernatural threat
groups.explanation: Patience, Wyoming (Big Sky / Wynonna Earp), Beacon Hills (Teen Wolf), Mystic Falls (The Vampire Diaries), and Hawkins, Indiana (Stranger Things) are all fictional small towns whose entire narrative centers on a supernatural or paranormal threat that the townspeople must confront.

groups.name: Openly gay actors who played straight lead characters in prestige or network dramas
groups.explanation: Jim Parsons (Sheldon Cooper in The Big Bang Theory), Neil Patrick Harris (Barney Stinson in How I Met Your Mother), Matt Bomer (Neal Caffrey in White Collar), and Zachary Quinto (Spock in assorted roles / Dr. Oliver Thredson in American Horror Story) are all publicly gay actors who played canonically straight leading characters.

groups.name: TV show titles that are also real U.S. geographic or natural landmarks
groups.explanation: Rust Belt (a real U.S. geographic region — the show Rust Belt exists), Yellowstone (the national park and river — also the Paramount drama), The Wire (a method of communication — also a geographic infrastructure term, and the HBO show), and Empire (Empire State — refers to New York as a geographic identity, also the Fox drama). Each show title doubles as a real and recognized U.S. geographic or infrastructural term or place.

groups.name: Things associated with the TV show Treme that also appear elsewhere on this board as red herrings
groups.explanation: These four tiles are the trap group. 'I have a type. Brilliant, a little broken.' is a quote from Treme character Janette Desautel. Seymour is the name of a character in Treme. Treme is itself a tile (the show title). Tulsa King — 'Tulsa' echoes the jazz/music world Treme inhabits, and 'King' references the real New Orleans tradition of Mardi Gras Indians (Big Chiefs/Kings) central to Treme's plot. These tiles seem to scatter across different shows but all have a specific Treme connection: quote, character name, show title, and thematic reference to the show's core Mardi Gras Indian royalty tradition.
